Mou Anju Door Industry Co., Ltd. v. Sichuan Mou Door Industry Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of trademark rights and unfair competition

Ruling Gist

Where a party, knowing full well the reputation and influence of another's registered trademark and trade name, still extensively uses trademarks similar to the other's registered trademark in conducting the same business, such party has the malicious intent to free-ride on the other's reputation. Where the scale of infringement is large, the scope of regions involved is extensive, and the profits from infringement are substantial, the infringement circumstances are severe. The people's court may, upon the request of the right holder, apply punitive damages by comprehensively considering factors such as the subjective fault of the infringer and the severity of the infringing circumstances.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Appeal No. 209

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Sichuan Mou Door Industry Co., Ltd. (formerly Sichuan XinMou Door Industry Co., Ltd.). Domicile: Pengxi County, Suining City, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Mou, Executive Director of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Hao, attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Jing, attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Chengdu Xindu District Wanxiang GuMou Metal Door Factory. Domicile: Xindu District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

Operator: Zhou Mou.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Hao, attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yanrong, trainee attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Zhou Mou, male, Han nationality.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Hao, attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Jing, attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Mou Anju Door Industry Co., Ltd. Domicile: Dashiqiao City, Yingkou City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: S*, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Kefeng, attorney at Beijing Jiren (Shanghai) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lv Pei, attorney at Beijing Jiren (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Fang Mou, female, Han nationality.

In the case of dispute over infringement of trademark rights and unfair competition between the appellants Sichuan Mou Door Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mou Door Industry Company), Chengdu Xindu District Wanxiang GuMou Metal Door Factory (hereinafter referred to as GuMou Door Factory), and Zhou Mou, and the appellee Mou Anju Door Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mou Anju Company), and the defendant at first instance Fang Mou, the appellants appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2018) Su Min Chu No. 38 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the original trial court) on October 13, 2021. This Court accepted the case on May 6, 2022, and formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law. The case was publicly heard on October 27, 2022, and July 3, 2023, respectively. The agents ad litem of Mou Door Industry Company and Zhou Mou, Zhang Hao and Li Jing, the agent ad litem of GuMou Door Factory, Zhang Hao and Chen Yanrong, and the agents ad litem of Mou Anju Company, Zhao Kefeng and Lv Pei, appeared in court for the hearing. The defendant at first instance, Fang Mou, was lawfully summoned but did not appear, and this Court held the trial by default. The case is now concluded.

Mou Door Industry Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou appealed requesting: 1. To set aside the original trial judgment; 2. To dismiss all claims of Mou Anju Company; 3. The litigation costs for the first and second instances to be borne by Mou Anju Company; 4. Order Mou Anju Company to compensate Mou Door Industry Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou for economic losses and reasonable expenses. Their reasons are as follows: (I) Sichuan XinMou Door Industry Co., Ltd. (the predecessor of Mou Door Industry Company, hereinafter referred to as XinMou Company), GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou had no malicious intent to free-ride on the reputation and influence of the series of trademarks involved in Mou Anju Company's case. Their production and sale of XinPanpan products did not constitute trademark infringement. The original trial court's findings of fact and application of law were erroneous and should be corrected. The alleged infringing acts claimed by Mou Anju Company occurred before the Beijing High People's Court rendered the second-instance administrative judgment. At that time, the trademark No. 1007** "XinPanpan" owned or licensed to XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou was still a legally valid registered trademark. Their use of the registered trademark in a standardized manner does not constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use the series of trademarks involved in Mou Anju Company's case. On July 15, 2016, Zhou Mou entered into a trademark assignment agreement with third party Zhang Mou to acquire the "XinPanpan" trademark. On September 13, 2016, Zhou Mou entered into a trademark license agreement with XinMou Company, licensing XinMou Company to use the trademark for a term until December 13, 2022. On November 17, 2017, the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Review Board) issued a ruling on an invalidation request, declaring the trademark No. 1007 "XinPanpan" invalid for goods including "mobile metal structures; metal doors; metal gates; metal windows," but maintained it for other goods. Zhou Mou, dissatisfied with the ruling, sued in the Beijing Intellectual Property Court, which rendered a first-instance administrative judgment setting aside the above ruling. Mou Anju Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court, which rendered a second-instance administrative judgment setting aside the first-instance judgment and dismissing Zhou Mou's claim. Although the "XinPanpan" trademark of Zhou Mou was declared invalid, a subsequent invalidation declaration cannot be used to entirely negate the prior lawful and normal use. The "XinPanpan" trademark and Mou Anju Company's trademarks No. 64 "" and No. 1079 "" have obvious differences in shape design, character composition, and pronunciation, making it difficult for ordinary consumers to consider them similar. Mou Anju Company's trademark is a combination of "PANPAN Panpan," which differs in pronunciation from "XinPanpan" and would not cause confusion. The character "Xin" in the "XinPanpan" trademark has many strokes, visually occupying most of the space of the trademark; the trademark emphasizes the character "Xin" rather than "Panpan." The "PANPAN Panpan" trademark and design of Mou Anju Company give more prominence to the preceding letters. The two can be easily distinguished. The words "Panpan" should belong to public resources. The mascot of the 1990 Beijing Asian Games, a panda, was widely promoted under the name "Panpan." The word "Panpan" is widely known and has high recognition among Chinese consumers. Mou Anju Company obtained registered trademarks containing the word "Panpan" by "free-riding on popularity," but the word "Panpan" is not exclusive to Mou Anju Company, nor can it monopolize the right to use the word "Panpan." Mou Anju Company has the right to restrict others from using its trademarks No. 64 "" and No. 1079 "", but it does not have the right to restrict others from using the word "Panpan." Therefore, the use by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou of the trademark "XinMou" containing the word "Panpan" or the enterprise name "Sichuan XinMou Door Industry Co., Ltd." containing the word "Panpan" does not constitute free-riding on Mou Anju Company's series of trademarks or goodwill, nor does it infringe on its trademark rights. The use by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou prior to the invalidation of the "XinPanpan" trademark was not subjectively wrongful. The "XinPanpan" trademark was filed by a third party, and the third party's application for registration did not have the malicious intent to free-ride on Mou Anju Company's prior trademark reputation. Zhou Mou and XinMou Company had no malicious intent when Zhou Mou acquired the "XinPanpan" trademark and when XinMou Company was licensed to use it. After obtaining the trademark right, their use was based on reliance on the authorization of the trademark administrative authority. After the "XinPanpan" trademark was declared invalid, Zhou Mou terminated the trademark license to XinMou Company, and XinMou Company also terminated the entrusted processing relationship with GuMou Door Factory. XinMou Company also repeatedly demanded that distributors not continue to use the "XinPanpan" trademark. (II) The actions of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou do not constitute unfair competition. The use of the "XinPanpan" trademark and enterprise name by XinMou Company and GuMou Door Factory in their operations does not constitute free-riding on Mou Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name. Subjectively, XinMou Company and GuMou Door Factory used the licensed "XinPanpan" trademark, which was lawful use of a registered trademark, and they had no subjective intent to free-ride on the "Panpan" trade name. The panda image used by XinMou Company and GuMou Door Factory was designed independently by a third-party design company commissioned by them, and it is not similar to Mou Anju Company's panda graphic, nor would it cause consumer confusion. The promotional activities of XinMou Company and GuMou Door Factory do not constitute false advertising or commercial disparagement. Any promotional activities by distributors, even if true, were the individual actions of the distributors. (III) The original trial court erred in identifying the entities liable for damages; Zhou Mou and GuMou Door Factory should not bear liability or joint liability. Even if liability is imposed, it should only be joint liability for some acts. In the trademark infringement dispute, Zhou Mou was the assignee of the "XinPanpan" trademark, and there was no indication that he knew the trademark was infringing at the time of assignment. He should not bear liability or joint liability for damages from all unfair competition acts. GuMou Door Factory accepted entrusted processing from XinMou Company to produce steel door series products, which does not constitute trademark infringement. GuMou Door Factory was not the subject of the alleged unfair competition acts, so it should not bear liability or joint liability. (IV) The original trial court's determination of damages liability was clearly erroneous and should be corrected. The original trial court's findings on intentional infringement, severe circumstances, and the basis for calculating damages for XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou were erroneous. Punitive damages should not apply to the alleged trademark infringement acts. Although both the "XinPanpan" trademark and Mou Anju Company's trademark No. 64** "" contain the two Chinese characters "Panpan," there are significant differences in pronunciation, overall composition, and visual effect between the two trademarks, and the degree of similarity is not high. Although the "XinPanpan" trademark was ultimately declared invalid, it should be noted that the case went through invalidation, first instance, second instance, and retrial, with inconsistent conclusions at different stages. The Beijing Intellectual Property Court set aside the administrative ruling on the ground that the two trademarks were not similar for identical or similar goods. Zhou Mou is an ordinary person, not a trademark professional, and it is difficult for him to determine whether the two trademarks are similar. Therefore, the ultimate invalidation of the "XinPanpan" trademark cannot be used to retroactively infer that Zhou Mou knew of the infringement of Mou Anju Company's trademark rights at the time of purchasing and using the "XinPanpan" trademark, showing clear intent. The alleged trademark infringement does not constitute "severe circumstances." XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou used the "XinPanpan" trademark in a standardized manner, without exceeding the scope of approved goods, changing the distinctive features, or splitting or combining the trademark. This does not meet the threshold of "severe circumstances" for applying punitive damages. The scale of operation and the actual scope of business of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou were small, and their profits were low; they were not "large-scale and wide-ranging" as found by the original trial court. The expected targets in external promotional and agency contracts cannot be directly used as a basis for determining profits. After the "XinPanpan" trademark was declared invalid by an effective judgment, XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou stopped using the trademark. Even if punitive damages were to be applied, the original trial court's determination of the calculation base for trademark punitive damages was erroneous and lacked factual basis. Its calculation method was subjective and unfounded. The evidence submitted by Mou Anju Company to prove the relevant facts was doubtful as to its authenticity. The annual procurement target increase of at least 50% mentioned in the above evidence was only an expected target in the contract, and there is no evidence that the contract was performed as agreed. Since XinMou Company began using the "XinPanpan" trademark, it was still in a preliminary investment and preparation phase, with unsatisfactory business conditions. Moreover, after the "XinPanpan" trademark was later declared invalid, distributors demanded termination and compensation. XinMou Company quickly fell into paralysis with no actual profit. Therefore, the original trial court's determination of the damages base as RMB 34,271,200 lacked factual basis. In summary, there is no basis for applying punitive damages in this case, and the original trial court's application was clearly erroneous. The damages for unfair competition awarded by the original trial court were clearly excessive. The reasonable expenses supported by the original trial court were not necessary expenses incurred by Mou Anju Company for initiating this lawsuit and were clearly excessive.

Mou Anju Company argued in defense that the original registrant of the "XinPanpan" trademark had no connection with the alleged trademark infringement and unfair competition acts, and Mou Anju Company did not intend to pursue the original registrant's liability. The original trial court's finding of facts on the alleged trademark infringement by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou was clear and should be upheld. The "XinPanpan" trademark was declared invalid, which should produce an effect of invalidity ab initio. XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou used various forms of the "XinPanpan" mark, including many variations that highlight the "Panpan" part, creating confusing similarity with Mou Anju Company's series of trademarks. Their use of the "XinPanpan" trademark showed clear malicious intent to free-ride on Mou Anju Company's prior series of trademarks with high reputation, and their use before the invalidation of the "XinPanpan" trademark constituted trademark infringement. The use by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou of the "XinPanpan" enterprise name, abbreviation, trade name, and panda mascot image caused confusion among the relevant public. Additionally, there were various acts of false advertising and commercial disparagement of Mou Anju Company's brand through WeChat public account texts, Moments, and group chats. The original trial court's finding that their actions constituted unfair competition had factual basis. Furthermore, regarding the determination of damages: XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou had significant intentional infringement, extremely severe circumstances, and were dilatory in providing evidence, so they should bear adverse consequences. The original trial court fully considered that Mou Anju Company had done its best to provide evidence and could only reasonably estimate the infringing profits based on some product sales contracts submitted by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou and their own statements on product sales scale, to determine the calculation base for punitive damages. The final application of a five-times punitive damages multiplier to determine the amount of damages for trademark infringement was scientifically sound. Given the extremely large scale of unfair competition acts by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou, their obvious malicious intent, and the variety of acts, the original trial court's determination of damages of RMB 5,000,000 for unfair competition had legal basis. Mou Anju Company incurred necessary expenses to protect its rights, and the original trial court's determination of RMB 650,000 as reasonable expenses had factual basis. In summary, Mou Anju Company requested that the original trial judgment be affirmed and the appeals of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou be dismissed.

Mou Anju Company filed a lawsuit with the original trial court, requesting the following: 1. Order XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou to immediately cease the alleged infringing acts infringing on Mou Anju Company's series of trademarks involved (including well-known marks), and to cancel or transfer the infringing domain names to Mou Anju Company. 2. Order XinMou Company to immediately cease using the enterprise name "XinPanpan" that is similar to Mou Anju Company's trade name, and to undergo name change registration; order XinMou Company to immediately cease using the panda mascot image in its business promotion activities and the unfair competition acts of free-riding on Mou Anju Company's "Panpan" brand goodwill; order cessation of the alleged false advertising acts; order Zhou Mou to immediately cease the alleged commercial disparagement acts. 3. Order XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou to publish a statement in the China Market Supervision News to eliminate the impact. 4. Order Fang Mou to immediately cease selling and promoting the infringing products produced by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou; to cease using infringing signs such as "XinPanpan Chaoshuo" and "Panpan Chaoshuo" in store decorations, promotional materials, store signs, and business cards; and to cease providing other assistance for the infringing acts of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou. 5. Order XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou to jointly and severally compensate Mou Anju Company RMB 100,000,000, and order Fang Mou to bear joint and several liability with XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou within the range of RMB 3,000,000. Order XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou to jointly and severally compensate Mou Anju Company for reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringing acts, totaling RMB 898,212.52, and order Fang Mou to bear joint and several liability with XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou Mou for the above reasonable expenses within the range of RMB 100,000. During the trial, after Fang Mou apologized, Mou Anju Company only requested that Fang Mou bear RMB 51,000 in compensation for reasonable expenses. 6. Order XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, Zhou Mou, and Fang Mou to jointly and severally bear the litigation costs of this case.

The original trial court found the following facts:

(I) Mou Anju Company’s registration, business conditions, registration of the series of trademarks involved, level of recognition, and protection record

The predecessor of Mou Anju Company, Liaoning Moumou Group Co., Ltd., was established on September 13, 1996, with a business scope including anti-theft doors and windows, file cabinets, etc. On January 15, 2002, the group company was restructured through a shareholding reform into Moumou Anju Co., Ltd., and on September 30, 2009, it changed to its current name and has continued to operate to the present. The business scope includes the production, research and development, sale, and installation of anti-theft doors and windows, security doors and windows, fireproof doors and windows, entrance doors, interior doors, garage doors, wooden doors, metal doors and windows, door and window locks, and supporting products for various products and hardware products. From 2009, Mou Anju Company had a huge scale of operations, with operating revenue of nearly RMB 1.2 billion in 2009, reaching RMB 1.8 billion in 2014, and continuing to grow.

On July 10, 1992, the ChangMou Metal Products Factory of Yingkou City, Liaoning Province, applied for registration of trademark No. 64**** "" on goods in Class 6 such as "safes; anti-theft doors," which was approved on June 28, 1993. On September 7, 1999, it was transferred to Liaoning Moumou Group Co., Ltd. after approval. Following renewal, the trademark is valid until June 27, 2023.

On January 20, 1998, Mou Anju Company applied for registration of trademark No. 130**** "" on goods in Class 6 such as "metal doors; metal windows; metal cabinets; safe boxes; metal locks; metal alloy doors," which was approved on August 7, 1999. Following renewal, the trademark is valid until August 6, 2029.

On January 7, 1999, Mou Anju Company applied for registration of trademark No. 140**** "" on goods in Class 6 such as "metal doors; metal windows; window frames; iron products for doors; metal locks (non-electric)," which was approved on May 28, 2000. Following renewal, the trademark is valid until May 27, 2030.

On April 19, 2012, Mou Anju Company applied for registration of trademark No. 1079**** "" on goods in Class 6 such as "metal doors; metal windows; window frames; iron products for doors; metal locks (non-electric)," which was approved on June 28, 2013. The term of exclusive right to use the trademark is valid until June 27, 2023.

On December 29, 1999, the Trademark Office of the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Office) recognized trademark No. 64** "" and trademark No. 130** "" (PANPAN and panda graphic trademark) as well-known trademarks on anti-theft door goods in Class 6.

Given that the trademarks No. 64** and No. 1079** of Mou Anju Company had prior reputation, there existed a large number of trademarks on the market that imitatively preemptively registered "Panpan" or sought to free-ride on the goodwill of Mou Anju Company and its "Panpan" brand. Mou Anju Company continuously monitored and actively initiated trademark oppositions, applications for revocation of trademarks unused for three consecutive years, civil litigation, administrative enforcement, criminal enforcement, and other procedures to take rights protection measures, and obtained support and recognition in the rulings of the China National Intellectual Property Administration, the Shandong High People's Court, the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province, the Wuling District People's Court of Changde, Hunan Province, and the Market Supervision Administration of Hong'an County, Hubei Province.

On August 13, 2019, the China National Intellectual Property Administration, in its rulings on invalidation request Nos. 190250 and 190252 (2019), determined that the trademark No. 1079** ("Panpan PANPAN and design") had a well-known status in the goods of metal doors and security doors, and declared the trademarks No. 2396 and No. 2397** "Xin Panpan" of Zhou to be invalid.

On July 4, 2019, the China National Intellectual Property Administration, in ten decisions refusing to register the "Xin Panpan" word marks applied for by Zhou, determined the well-known status of Mou Anju Company's trademark No. 1079**** ("Panpan PANPAN and design") on the goods "security doors," and considered that Chengdu Wanxiang Gu Mou Technology Co., Ltd., for which Zhou served as the legal representative, had business dealings with Mou Anju Company as early as 2007, but established Xin Mou Company in 2016 and applied for registration of numerous "Xin Panpan" trademarks in multiple classes of goods and services, and that such conduct clearly manifested subjective bad faith in free-riding on the reputation and influence of Mou Anju Company.

Since 2017, the China National Intellectual Property Administration and the Beijing Intellectual Property Court have, in at least 32 opposition decisions, invalidation rulings, and administrative judgments, determined the well-known trademark status of the trademarks No. 64** and No. 1079** ("Panpan PANPAN and design"), and on that basis refused to register subsequently applied-for trademarks such as "Panpan Qiyue," "Ping'an Panpan," "Panpan Jintaiyang," "Yiju Panpan," "Qinglin Panpan Yipin," and "Huaxia Panpan."

(2) Information regarding the publicity, product market share, and honors received by Mou Anju Company for its enterprise and the series of trademarks involved

Since 1992, Mou Anju Company and its affiliated companies have invested huge sums annually in continuous, extensive publicity and promotion of the "Panpan" enterprise and its series of trademarks involved through various channels such as television advertisements, newspapers and magazines, outdoor advertising, and products sold, covering all parts of the country and diverse audience groups. Starting in 2009, the annual investment in publicity and promotion by Mou Anju Company and its subsidiaries exceeded RMB 10 million, exceeded RMB 20 million in 2014, and exceeded RMB 18 million in 2015. This included continuous, in-depth, and extensive publicity and reporting on Mou Anju Company and its series of trademarks involved on national and industry heavyweight print media platforms such as People's Daily, Economic Daily, Guangming Daily, Reference News, Science and Technology Daily, China Building Materials News, China Quality News, and China Consumer News; print media platforms reaching various regions such as Beijing Evening News and Yangcheng Evening News; television programs such as CCTV's "Chaowen Tianxia" and Tianjin TV's "Hunyin Baowei Zhan"; the "ASSA ABLOY Panpan" bullet train; and giant highway billboards.

From 1996 to 2012, for more than ten consecutive years, the National Bureau of Statistics, the China Technological Progress Information Distribution Center, the China Industry Enterprise Information Distribution Center, and other institutions issued honorary certificates, and the Public Security Ministry's Office for Security Technology Prevention Management and the China Security and Protection Industry Association issued certificates, clearly stating that Panpan brand security door products ranked first in terms of sales volume among similar products in the national market. At the same time, from 1995 to 2015, state institutions such as the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce, the former Ministry of Construction, and the National Bureau of Statistics, as well as industry associations such as the China Consumers' Association and the China Association for Quality Inspection, awarded Mou Anju Company and its products and brands at least 157 honors and awards, including "One of the 100 Chinese Famous Brands Going Global" and "Recommended Product for National Well-off Housing Construction."

(3) Relationship among Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang, and the alleged infringing acts

1. Registration status and interrelationship of Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang

Xin Mou Company was established on September 13, 2016, with a registered capital of RMB 3 million, with Zhou holding 80% of the shares and serving as the legal representative. During the litigation, on July 1, 2019, the legal representative of the company was changed to Zhou Jia, but Zhou still held 99% of the shares. The business scope of Xin Mou Company includes: production and sale of metal doors and windows, movable metal buildings, metal casings, steel plates, metal ropes, metal bolts, metal key chains, metal pulleys (not for machines), wood products, aluminum-wood doors and windows, steel products, fire doors (steel, wood, steel-wood), security doors, special doors, bathroom doors, ceilings, integrated home furnishing; sale of building materials, hardware, smart home; interior and exterior decoration; property leasing; property management.

Gu Mou Door Factory is an individually-owned business, with the operator being Zhou, established on May 15, 2006. Its business scope includes: manufacturing and installation of metal doors and windows, aluminum-plastic doors and windows; sale of building materials (excluding hazardous chemicals).

Zhu Mou Commercial Firm was established in November 2014, with the operator being Fang, as an individually-owned business, and was approved for cancellation on May 20, 2019.

Approved by the Trademark Office, on December 14, 2012, a third party, Zhang, registered the trademark "Xin Panpan," with registration certificate No. 1007****, approved for use on goods in class 6, such as steel plates, movable metal buildings, metal doors, metal gates, metal windows, etc. On July 15, 2016, Zhou and Zhang signed a trademark assignment agreement, and Zhou acquired the trademark, which was approved by the Trademark Office on February 13, 2017. On September 13, 2016, Zhou and Xin Mou Company signed a trademark license contract, licensing the "Xin Panpan" trademark to Xin Mou Company for a term until December 13, 2022. On the same day, Xin Mou Company and Gu Mou Door Factory signed a product entrustment processing agreement, whereby the former entrusted the latter to process steel door series products. On April 1, 2018, Xin Mou Company authorized Zhu Mou Commercial Firm to use the "Xin Panpan" trademark and authorized Fang as the general distributor for the Suzhou area.

Between October 31, 2016, and September 30, 2017, Xin Mou Company applied for design patents for products such as door frames, doors, fire doors, anti-pry doors, and security door locks, obtained authorization, and received corresponding rewards. Starting in April 2017, Xin Mou Company, by entering into agreements with others, ordering production equipment, entrusting design websites, brand image and store environment design, setting up factory direct experience halls and specialty stores, leasing and setting up exhibition booths, placing outdoor advertisements, filming and broadcasting TV programs and documentaries, and making donations, conducted offline and online publicity and promotion of Xin Mou Company and its "Xin Panpan" products and brands, engaging in business activities covering provinces, cities, and counties such as Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Chongqing, Beijing, Shaanxi, Shandong, Fujian, Hunan, Jiangxi, Henan, Zhejiang, etc. Some specialty store distribution contracts and direct-sale store contracting agreements were signed starting from April 2019 and October 2019, and some contract periods covered 2018, 2019, 2020, and 2021. In the agency contracts provided by Xin Mou Company with distributors, the vast majority stipulated that the annual target for picking up goods from Xin Mou Company would increase by at least over 50%, and a substantial portion stipulated a 100% annual increase in the pick-up target. During this period, in December 2016, Xin Mou Company received the "Online Polling Well-known Enterprise" from the Organizing Committee of the China Real Estate 2017 Annual Procurement Summit; in January and March 2017, its products were evaluated by the Sichuan Provincial Quality and Technology Supervision Information Center and the Sichuan Provincial Quality and Technology Supervision 12365 Name Protection and Anti-Counterfeiting Network as "Quality Inspection Qualified and Safety Compliant Products" and "Consumer Favorite Products." In January, May, and July 2017, its brand obtained honorary titles such as "China Door Industry (Steel Door) Gold Award," "Recommended Brand for China Door and Window Industry," and "Top Ten Brands in China Door Industry" from the China Building Decoration and Decoration Materials Association, the China International Famous Brand Development Promotion Committee, the National Quality Brand Strategy Promotion Federation, the China Product Quality Technology Supervision Center, and the China International Door Industry Exhibition.

2. Facts related to the alleged infringing acts

On June 21, 2018, through notarization, the agent of Mou Anju Company purchased a "Xin Panpan" security door product for RMB 13,970 from a store operated by Zhu Mou Commercial Firm with a sign reading "Xin Panpan Chaoshuo High-end Security Door." The business card of the owner Fang of Zhu Mou Commercial Firm and the staff uniforms bore the words "Panpan Chaoshuo." On July 2, 2018, through notarization, the agent of Mou Anju Company received the security door purchased from Zhu Mou Commercial Firm via notarization at the installation location in Shanghai. The outer packaging of the security door showed that the product was a high-end "Xin Panpan" brand security door and accessories shipped by Xin Mou Company to Fang, the owner of Zhu Mou Commercial Firm. The consignment notice for the product showed the consignor as "New Panpan." The product packaging indicated that the product was supervised and manufactured by Xin Mou Company, with the entrusted manufacturer being Gu Mou Door Factory, and bore the words "Xin Panpan," "XPP," "China Door Industry Gold Award," and "Top Ten Brands of Door Industry." On the security door and its protective film, there were also markings such as "Xin Panpan®," "XPP," "Xin Mou Company," "China Door Industry Top Ten Meritorious Figures," and "" logos. Scanning QR codes on the product packaging and affixed to the security door product via WeChat allowed access to the WeChat public account of Xin Mou Company. Brochures sent with the goods stated, "Xin Panpan Craftsman Door positions itself as China's door and window craftsman, with a total investment of RMB 2 billion, owning six wholly-owned, equity-participated, controlling, and shared door companies, twelve wooden door companies..., with a total planned area of 1 million square meters, currently having 3 million security doors..., 2 million sets of matching wooden doors..., possessing three major bases," "Jointly developed with the large door equipment manufacturer New Century, a fully automatic full-groove Marshal frame production line with a daily output of 10,000 high-end series, first in China. The wooden door company jointly introduced a fully automated production line with a daily output of 4,000 solid wooden doors, the largest single-factory daily output in China. The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether Zhou is a proper defendant in this case; 2. Whether the alleged acts constitute infringement of Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case and unfair competition; 3. If so, whether and how Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang should bear legal liability.

The court of first instance held that, as the alleged infringing acts in this case were ongoing in 2019, the nature of the relevant acts and legal liability should be determined in accordance with the 2019 revised Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law) and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law).

(I) Zhou is a proper defendant in this case.

Although Zhou acquired the "Xin Panpan" trademark from a third party, Anju Company sued Zhou on the grounds that Zhou maliciously acquired the trademark, maliciously licensed Xin Company to use the trademark, violated legal provisions by engaging in commercial defamation, and as a former legal representative and actual controller of Xin Company and the person in charge of Gu Door Factory, should bear legal liability for the two companies' malicious use of the allegedly infringing identifiers. Specifically, Anju Company claimed that Zhou not only independently engaged in commercial defamation but also had the subjective intent to use the companies under his control to commit trademark infringement and unfair competition, and jointly committed the infringing acts with Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and others. Therefore, Zhou is a proper defendant in this case.

(II) The alleged trademark infringement acts claimed by Anju Company are established.

Xin Company and Gu Door Factory, in the production and sale of goods and their packaging, in-store decoration, domain names, and in the promotional media involved in the case, used business identifiers such as the Chinese characters "Panpan," the pinyin "PANPAN" and its abbreviations, and the panda graphic, which are associated with Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case. Zhu Commercial Firm sold the allegedly infringing products. These acts all constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case.

1. Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case have a very high reputation, reaching the level of well-known marks. (1) Anju Company has continuously produced and sold security doors and other products under the "Panpan" trade name for over 20 years, with an enormous scale of operations, products covering the whole country, and its security door product sales volume and market share have ranked first in the industry for over 20 consecutive years, enjoying a very high reputation among consumers. (2) The series of trademarks involved in the case have been registered and used in China for over 20 years. As early as December 29, 1999, Trademark No. 64** " " and Trademark No. 130 " " (PANPAN and panda graphic) were recognized by the Trademark Office as well-known trademarks for security door goods in Class 6. From 2017 until the period of this litigation, in relevant administrative dispute rulings and judicial judgments, Trademark No. 64 " " and No. 1079** " " used on metal doors and security doors were repeatedly recognized as well-known trademarks or as having the status of well-known trademarks. (3) Since 1992, Anju Company and its related companies have invested heavily in extensive nationwide publicity for Anju Company, its products, and the series of trademarks involved in the case through various channels such as high-speed rail, television, newspapers and magazines, and outdoor advertising. (4) Over the years, Anju Company, its products, and the series of trademarks involved in the case have received at least 157 awards and honors. (5) Anju Company has continuously filed oppositions, invalidation declarations, and rights enforcement actions against the trademark hoarding and use by Xin Company and others, and has received support and protection from administrative rulings and judicial judgments. Therefore, through Anju Company's continuous use, extensive publicity, and active rights enforcement, the series of trademarks involved in the case have achieved a very high reputation, goodwill, and influence in the goods of "security doors, metal doors, metal windows," reaching the status of well-known marks. This is also confirmed by the conclusions of the market perception survey report provided by Anju Company.

2. Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhu Commercial Firm prominently used identifiers such as the Chinese characters "Panpan," the pinyin "PANPAN" and its abbreviations, and the panda graphic, which are similar to those in the series of trademarks involved in the case, on goods and their packaging, in-store decoration, domain names, and in other business fields or promotional media. The four series of trademarks involved in the case that Anju Company seeks to protect in this case use the Chinese characters "Panpan," the pinyin "PANPAN," and the associated panda graphic as distinctive identifying elements, forming a customary way of calling out the "Panpan" characters and the "PANPAN" pinyin. In the two registered trademarks involving the panda graphic, the panda's left hand also holds the "Panpan" characters, "PANPAN" pinyin, and the overlapping pinyin abbreviation "P" graphic. Xin Company and Gu Door Factory used the allegedly infringing identifiers extensively in the production and sale of goods and their packaging; on their official website, WeChat public account, WeChat mini-programs, and APP; as the name of the WeChat public account; as the main part of the official website domain name in the form of a pinyin abbreviation; on the door or in-store decoration of Gu Door Factory's factory area and multiple offline stores operated by Xin Company, such as security smart experience centers; and in promotional materials, exhibitions, outdoor advertising, and other business and promotional activities. They publicized and promoted products or the enterprise itself, such as "Xin Panpan" security doors, wooden doors, metal doors and windows, aluminum alloy doors and windows, smart homes, sunrooms, and smart locks, and conducted business activities. 3. The goods produced and sold by Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhu Commercial Firm are identical, similar, or related to the goods for which Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case are approved for use. The security doors, wooden doors, metal doors and windows, aluminum alloy doors and windows, and smart locks operated by Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, Zhou, and Zhu Commercial Firm using the allegedly infringing Chinese characters, pinyin, panda graphic, and other business identifiers are identical or similar to Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case. Although the categories of goods or services for which Xin Company and Gu Door Factory use and promote smart homes, sunrooms, and other goods or services are not identical or similar, such use constitutes reproduction or imitation of Anju Company's well-known trademarks or their main parts.

4. The use of the above Chinese characters, identifiers, etc., by Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhu Commercial Firm caused confusion and mistaken belief among the relevant public. For a long time, the series of trademarks involved in the case have enjoyed a very high reputation and are well known to relevant consumers. The use of relevant Chinese characters, pinyin and its abbreviations, panda graphics, etc., by Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhu Commercial Firm is likely to cause the relevant public to be confused about the source of the products, or to mistakenly believe that there is an investment or operational cooperation or relationship between Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Anju Company.
