5. The intent of Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou to free ride on the goodwill and influence of Anju Company's trade name and the series of trademarks involved in the case is quite evident. This is mainly manifested in: (1) Anju Company was established and registered the series of trademarks involved in the case over 20 years ago, 20 years earlier than the establishment of Xin Company, and Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case have been continuously famous. The character "Xin" is homophonic for "new." Xin Company registered the trade name "Xin Panpan," used the characters "Xin Panpan," the pinyin or its abbreviations, related panda graphics, and promoted its own security door products as high-end products, upgraded products of the "Panpan" brand, etc., clearly intending to free ride on the commercial reputation of Anju Company and its registered trademarks, with a clear purpose of causing market confusion. (2) Evidence shows that Zhou has been engaged in the operation of security doors and windows and other products for many years. The company he served as legal representative, Chengdu Wanxiang Gu Mou Technology Co., Ltd., had business dealings with Anju Company as early as 2007. It can be determined that Zhou knew of the well-known degree and influence of Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name and the series of trademarks involved in the case, yet he established Xin Company in September 2016. On the day of establishment, Zhou authorized Xin Company to use the "Xin Panpan" trademark he had acquired, and Xin Company immediately commissioned Gu Door Factory to produce security doors and other metal door and window series products, engaging in the same business as Anju Company. (3) Zhou contacted Zhang, the original registrant of the "Xin Panpan" trademark, multiple times and acquired the trademark on July 15, 2016, and licensed it to Xin Company, in which he held a controlling stake and served as legal representative. Xin Company then commissioned Gu Door Factory to produce "Xin Panpan" security doors and other products. At the same time, he filed a large number of applications to register the "Xin Panpan" trademark in multiple goods and service categories. (4) Zhou knew on January 19, 2017, that Anju Company had filed an invalidation declaration request against the trademark No. 1007**** for "Xin Panpan" that he had acquired. He still instructed Xin Company, which he controlled, held a controlling stake in, and served as legal representative, to continue using the Chinese characters, pinyin or its abbreviations, panda graphics, abbreviations or trade names of company names, and other relevant identifiers from the series of trademarks involved in the case. Even after the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board issued an invalidation ruling on November 17, 2017, declaring the "Xin Panpan" trademark invalid, and after the Beijing High People's Court issued a final judgment on January 15, 2019, affirming the invalidation ruling of the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board, Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou continued to use the allegedly infringing identifiers. (5) On June 26, 2017, Xin Company registered the WeChat public account "Xin Panpan High-end Security Door." This public account was briefly renamed "Xin Pan Ming Pin Boutique Security Door" on May 6, 2019, but was renamed again to "Sichuan Xin Mou Company Ltd." on August 19, three months later. (6) Many distributors of Xin Company clearly stated that the reason they joined was that they valued the reputation of Anju Company and its series of trademarks involved in the case.

In summary, Xin Company and Gu Door Factory, in the production and sale of goods and their packaging, in-store decoration, domain names, other business activities, and the promotional media involved in the case, used business identifiers such as the Chinese characters "Panpan," the pinyin and its abbreviations, and the panda graphic, which are distinctive elements of the series of trademarks involved in the case. This constitutes malicious free-riding on and imitation of Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case, objectively causing significant damage to Anju Company's interests. Zhu Commercial Firm, knowing of Anju Company's well-known trademarks and failing to fulfill its duty of review, still sold the allegedly infringing products and used the characters "Panpan" on its storefront and business cards. All these acts constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case.

Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou argued that they lawfully acquired the "Xin Panpan" trademark, had used and promoted the "Xin Panpan" brand since then, and their products had also obtained certain honors, so their use was a legitimate use of the trademark. The court of first instance held that, as stated above, Zhou's acquisition of the "Xin Panpan" trademark and the use of relevant identifiers by Xin Company and Gu Door Factory clearly demonstrated the intent to free ride on the commercial reputation of Anju Company and its trademarks. Moreover, the honors they obtained and their use of the "Xin Panpan" trademark occurred only in 2016 and 2017, after the acquisition of the trademark and the establishment of Xin Company in 2016, whereas Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case were registered over 20 years ago and have continuously enjoyed a very high reputation. Therefore, their defense lacked factual and legal basis, and the court of first instance did not support it.

(III) The alleged unfair competition acts claimed by Anju Company are established.

1. Under Zhou's control and instruction, Xin Company's registration and Xin Company's and Gu Door Factory's use of Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name in their operations constitute unfair competition. Anju Company registered the "Panpan" trade name in 1996 and has continuously produced and sold "Panpan" brand security doors and other products to this day, with an enormous scale of operations, products covering the whole country, and its security door product sales volume and market share have ranked first in the industry for nearly 20 consecutive years, enjoying a very high reputation among consumers. Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case have been registered and used in China for over 20 years and have continuously enjoyed a very high reputation. Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name and the series of trademarks involved in the case have interacted and influenced each other in use and publicity, continuously enhancing their reputation and influence. Zhou had business dealings with Anju Company as early as 2007. Knowing of the well-known degree and influence of Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name and the series of trademarks involved in the case, he acquired another person's "Xin Panpan" trademark in July 2016 and established Xin Company in September 2016. On the day of establishment, Zhou authorized Xin Company to use the "Xin Panpan" trademark he had acquired, and Xin Company immediately commissioned Gu Door Factory to produce security doors and other metal door and window series products. Xin Company and Gu Door Factory, controlled by Zhou, deliberately used the "Xin Panpan" enterprise name, its abbreviations, and trade names on products or in other business activities, engaging in the same business as Anju Company. This clearly demonstrates the subjective intent to free ride on Anju Company's "Panpan" enterprise name and the series of trademarks involved in the case, which have a very high reputation and influence, and objectively caused confusion and mistaken belief among the relevant public. This violates the above legal provisions and constitutes unfair competition.

2. The extensive use of the panda mascot image by Xin Company and Gu Door Factory in their operations and promotional activities constitutes unfair competition. Through over 20 years of continuous promotion and use by Anju Company, the "PANPAN" and panda graphic trademarks of Anju Company have reached the level of well-known marks, and are closely associated with Anju Company and its security doors and other products. The panda graphic or image has become a distinctive feature and main identifying element of its trademarks. When seeing a panda graphic on security doors, metal doors, or metal window products, the relevant public would naturally associate it with Anju Company and its "Panpan" brand. As stated above, Xin Company and Gu Door Factory, knowing the reputation, influence, and close association of this graphic trademark with Anju Company, still used the panda mascot image extensively on products, both online and offline, in operations and promotions, to promote security doors, metal doors and windows, and other products identical to Anju Company's. This panda mascot image is very close to Anju Company's "PANPAN" and panda graphic trademark in terms of posture, expression, and even the direction and angle of the head tilt. The use by Xin Company and Gu Door Factory is clearly for the purpose of free riding on Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case and its commercial goodwill, inducing consumers to become confused or mistaken. This violates the confusing acts stipulated in Article 6(4) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and constitutes unfair competition.

3. The misleading publicity conducted by Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory in this case constituted unfair competition through false advertising. The false advertising by Xinmou Company was manifested in the following: (1) Xinmou Company was established on September 13, 2016, and began using the "Xin Panpan" trademark to produce and sell anti-theft doors and related products in 2017. However, it prominently displayed "SINCE1998" on its official website, WeChat public account, and other conspicuous locations, thereby deceiving and misleading consumers into believing that its "Xin Panpan" brand had a history of over 20 years in anti-theft doors and metal doors. (2) Xinmou Company and Mou Anju Company were two independent business entities that had never collaborated in investment or operations. Nevertheless, the Administrative Director of Xinmou Company's "Shared Cloud Installation Group" and several distributors, in the course of their business promotion, consistently publicized that Xinmou Company and Mou Anju Company were previously the same entity and later separated, and that Xinmou Company operated high-end and upgraded products of the Panpan brand, thereby making false statements about the relationship between Mou Anju Company and Xinmou Company, as well as about Xinmou Company's operations and brand history. (3) The registration of Xinmou Company's Trademark No. 1007****, "Xin Panpan," for use on "metal doors, metal gates, metal windows, and movable metal buildings" was declared invalid by public announcement on February 27, 2019, and the exclusive right to use this registered trademark was deemed never to have existed. Thereafter, Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory continued to mark "Xin Panpan" as a registered trademark in the form of "Xin Panpan®" on goods such as metal doors, anti-theft doors, and metal windows. Meanwhile, they had not obtained trademark registration for goods or services in Classes 9, 19, and 37, yet they marked unregistered trademarks as registered trademarks in the form of "Xin Panpan®" on wooden doors, smart home products, smart locks, sunrooms, and related services. The aforementioned false representations by Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory demonstrated a clear subjective intent to improperly attach themselves to the well-known reputation, influence, and commercial goodwill of Mou Anju Company and its series of trademarks involved in the case, intending to lead the relevant public to believe that Xinmou Company had historical ties or connections with Mou Anju Company and its brands, thereby causing confusion and misunderstanding that the two parties had business dealings or cooperative investments and operations, thus improperly enhancing their own competitive advantage. Therefore, the above conduct violated Article 8 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and constituted unfair competition through false advertising.

4. Xinmou Company and Zhou engaged in commercial defamation against Mou Anju Company. Xinmou Company published on its official website and WeChat public account a "Notice on the Formal Rights Protection of the Xin Panpan® Trademark," claiming that there appeared on the market "Panpan" marks or combinations of "Panpan" with designs and letters, which "imitate Xin Panpan, a Chinese national brand and a well-known brand in the door industry, misleading Chinese consumers, openly publicizing the registered 'Panpan' trademark, and maliciously altering it to Panpan Security Doors and Panpan Anti-theft Doors. This seriously violates the principle of standardized use of registered trademarks under the Trademark Law." It listed Mou Anju Company's " ", "Panda Panpan," and other trademarks as trademarks that infringed upon, imitated, were similar to, or violated the "Xin Panpan" trademark. Zhou sent to the WeChat group "Sichuan Door Industry Association Boss Club" information regarding the trademark invalidation procedures he had initiated against Mou Anju Company's Trademark No. 1870** "Panpan Shangpin," Trademark No. 1579 "Panpan Yipin," and Trademark No. 1079** "Panpan," and commented, "Imperialism will always only fail, and will always be nothing but a paper tiger." Additionally, in the WeChat group "Sichuan Province Door Industry Association" and on his Moments, Zhou commented, "Warm congratulations to Xin Panpan trademark for its complete victory in Beijing. Everyone must share and promote this. Everyone should hold your head high and sell Xin Panpan anti-theft doors with integrity. It is a high-end series and first-line brand of Chinese national brands. Warm congratulations to Xin Panpan for its complete victory in the non-use revocation case at the National Trademark Office... The Chinese people's own national brand Xin Panpan will win, win, win!" and "True gold fears no fire." These actions directly targeted Mou Anju Company's legitimate use and promotion of the series of trademarks involved in the case, as well as its legally filed application to declare the "Xin Panpan" trademark invalid. They disseminated false information to consumers, seriously defaming Mou Anju Company's commercial reputation, the brand image of "Panpan," and the product reputation of "Panpan" anti-theft doors, thereby constituting the unfair competition act of commercial defamation.

(IV) Joint Infringement by Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory

Article 8 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where two or more persons jointly commit an act of infringement and cause damage to others, they shall be jointly and severally liable. Zhou intentionally attached himself to the well-known reputation and influence of Mou Anju Company's trade name and the series of trademarks involved in the case. He acquired the trademark from a third party, established and held a controlling interest in Xinmou Company, served as its legal representative, authorized Xinmou Company to use the "Xin Panpan" trademark, and Xinmou Company entrusted Gumou Door Factory to produce infringing products. Zhou was the private proprietor of Gumou Door Factory. Zhou directly controlled Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory in their business operations, directed the use of the allegedly infringing marks, and engaged in the relevant unfair competition acts. The intent and actions of Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou in committing the infringement were joint. Thus, the three parties constituted joint infringement.

(V) Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, Zhou, and Zhumou Commercial Firm Shall Bear Corresponding Legal Liability According to Law

Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, Zhou, and Zhumou Commercial Firm shall, according to law, bear civil liability for the infringement of the series of trademark rights involved in the case and the unfair competition acts, including cessation of infringement, elimination of adverse effects, and compensation for losses.

1. Regarding Cessation of Infringement and Elimination of Adverse Effects

Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory shall cease using commercial marks associated with the series of trademarks involved in the case, including the Chinese characters "盼盼" (Panpan), the pinyin "PANPAN" and its abbreviations, and the panda graphic, on the products they produce and sell, on the packaging thereof, in in-store decorations, in domain names, and in other business activities and promotional media. Zhumou Commercial Firm shall cease selling anti-theft doors and other goods bearing the above text or marks, and shall cease using the above text or marks in the decorations of its business premises. Xinmou Company adopted the abbreviation of the pinyin "PANPAN," the main element of Mou Anju Company's well-known trademark, as the main part of its website domain name, causing market confusion, and shall therefore cancel such domain name according to law.

Under the control and direction of Zhou, Xinmou Company registered its enterprise name, and together with Gumou Door Factory, used Mou Anju Company's trade name "Panpan," the panda mascot image, on the products they produced and sold, as well as in other business operations and promotions, and engaged in false advertising. Zhou and Xinmou Company committed commercial defamation against Mou Anju Company and other unfair competition acts. They shall cease the aforementioned infringing acts according to law. However, Mou Anju Company's claims only requested that Xinmou Company cease using the enterprise name containing the "Panpan" trade name and the panda mascot image, cease false advertising, and that Zhou cease commercial defamation. The court of first instance granted these requests. Xinmou Company shall also change its enterprise name, and the changed enterprise name shall not contain the words "Panpan."

Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou intentionally attached themselves to the well-known reputation, influence, and commercial goodwill of Mou Anju Company and its series of registered trademarks involved in the case, and engaged in trademark infringement and unfair competition, causing confusion and misidentification among the relevant public, seriously damaging the rights and interests of Mou Anju Company based on its well-known trade name and well-known trademarks. They shall bear the civil liability of eliminating the adverse effects. Mou Anju Company's request to publish a statement and eliminate adverse effects in the China Market Regulation News has factual and legal basis.

2. Regarding Compensation for Damages

(1) Determination of the Amount of Damages for Infringement of the Exclusive Right to Use a Registered Trademark

In this case, Mou Anju Company requested that the amount of compensation be determined based on the profits obtained by Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang from the infringement, and that punitive damages be applied according to law.

The court of first instance held that punitive damages should be applied in this case according to law. First, Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory had clear intent to infringe. As previously discussed, Zhou had engaged in the production and sale of anti-theft doors and similar products for a long time, had business dealings with Mou Anju Company as early as 2007, and had long known that Mou Anju Company's series of trademarks involved in the case were in a state of continuous well-known status. Nevertheless, he acquired the "Xin Panpan" trademark in July 2016, invested in and established Xinmou Company in September 2016, and became its controlling shareholder. On the very day of its establishment, Zhou authorized Xinmou Company to use the "Xin Panpan" trademark he had acquired, and Xinmou Company entrusted Gumou Door Factory to produce anti-theft doors and other metal door and window series products. Under the direct control and direction of Zhou, Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory used the allegedly infringing marks and engaged in the same business as Mou Anju Company. Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory used commercial marks related to "Panpan," including the Chinese characters, pinyin and its abbreviations, and the panda graphic, as well as enterprise names and abbreviations thereof, trade names, and the panda mascot image, on the products they produced and sold and their packaging, and in other business fields and promotional media. Their intent to attach themselves to the well-known reputation, influence, and commercial goodwill of Mou Anju Company's trade name and trademarks, and to deliberately cause market confusion and misidentification, was quite apparent. Moreover, after Mou Anju Company had repeatedly filed trademark disputes and invalidation applications, and after administrative rulings, administrative penalties, and court judgments had been issued, and even during the course of this litigation, the infringing acts of Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory continued unabated. The operational periods stipulated in relevant franchise contracts spanned 2019, 2020, and 2021. The purpose of Zhou's acquisition of the trademark, the establishment of Xinmou Company, and the entrustment of Gumou Door Factory by Xinmou Company was to attach themselves to the well-known reputation and influence of Mou Anju Company's trade name and trademarks to obtain huge profits, and they had from beginning to end derived huge illegal profits from the infringing business. Therefore, it can be determined that Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory made infringement their business, and thus all their sales profits shall be used to determine the infringing gains and the amount of compensation.

Second, the circumstances of infringement by Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang were quite serious. (1) Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory operated on a massive scale and across a wide area. After their establishment, they opened franchise stores and direct-sale stores nationwide, conducting online and offline business and promotions. The contracts they themselves provided showed that they had developed franchisees in twelve provinces, cities, and counties across the country, and their scale of operations and daily output were considerable. Their promotional brochures and official websites stated: "Xin Panpan Craftsman Door is positioned as a Chinese door and window craftsman, with a total investment of 2 billion yuan, owning six wholly-owned, share-participating, holding, and shared door industry companies, and twelve wooden door companies... with a total planned area of 1 million square meters, currently producing 3 million anti-theft doors..., supporting 2 million sets of wooden doors..., and possessing three major bases." "Jointly developed with the big company New Century, a Chinese door industry equipment supplier, the fully automatic full-groove Marshal frame production line, with a daily output of 10,000 high-quality series, the highest in China. The wooden door company jointly introduced a fully automated production line, with a daily output of 4,000 solid wood doors, the highest single-factory output of solid wood doors nationwide. The doors and windows introduced a fully automatic production line and assembly line from a German company Weige..., achieving automated management series for doors and windows, setting a model for China's Industry 4.0 door and window enterprises." "There are nearly 100 physical stores nationwide," etc. (2) They obtained huge profits from their operations. At Xinmou Company's "Xin Panpan Group 2018 New Product Annual Meeting and New Retail Summit Forum" in April 2018, more than 180 representatives of Xinmou Company's franchisees attended. Zhou stated that Xinmou Company planned to open one thousand enterprise pavilions within three years, achieve an output value of one billion yuan in the first five-year plan, and five billion yuan in the second five-year plan, and proposed to price products at a high level. These claims were roughly equivalent to the statement made by Jing, the Administrative Director of Xinmou Company's "Shared Cloud Installation Group," at the 2018 Beijing International Building Materials Exhibition, that the annual national sales of "Xin Panpan doors" amounted to 200 million yuan. The evidence provided by Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou showed that the total amount of distribution and agency contracts for Fujian Province, Beijing City, and Hunan Province from 2017 to 2019 alone was 50.6 million yuan. In the agency contracts provided by Xinmou Company with distributors, the vast majority stipulated that the annual target for goods withdrawal growth would be at least 50%, and a considerable portion stipulated that the target would increase by 100% annually. Considering the scale and scope of operations mentioned above, this indicates that the business plan proposed by Zhou was based on the existing huge production scale and substantial operating performance of Xinmou Company since its establishment. Since a people's court may determine the infringing gains based on relevant data from third-party commercial platforms, infringers' websites, promotional materials, or legally disclosed documents, and on industry average profit margins, the above publicly publicized content by Zhou and Xinmou Company regarding an output value of one billion yuan in the first five-year plan and five billion yuan in the second five-year plan is of certain reference value in calculating and determining the amount of compensation. (3) Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory made infringement their business. (4) Zhou knew on January 19, 2017, that Mou Anju Company had filed an application for invalidation of the "Xin Panpan" trademark (No. 1007****) he had acquired, yet he still instructed Xinmou Company and Gumou Door Factory, over which he held a controlling interest and served as legal representative and responsible person, to continue using the Chinese characters, pinyin and their abbreviations, panda graphic, and other related marks from the series of trademarks involved in the case. Even after the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board rendered an invalidation ruling on November 17, 2017, declaring the "Xin Panpan" trademark invalid, and after the Beijing High People's Court issued a final judgment on January 15, 2019, affirming the invalidation ruling of the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board, and even during the course of this litigation, Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou continued to use the series of trademarks involved in the case. (5) Zhou was well aware of the well-known status of Mou Anju Company's prior series of trademarks involved in the case. From May 2017 to September 17, 2019, Zhou still applied to register 36 "Xin Panpan" or similar trademarks in Classes 6, 9, 19, and other goods. In 2018, Zhou and Zhou Y, an employee of Xinmou Company, repeatedly filed malicious invalidation applications and applications for non-use revocation for three consecutive years against Mou Anju Company's previously registered trademarks. (6) This case involved Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou committing trademark infringement and multiple unfair competition acts, and they reproduced or imitated several of Mou Anju Company's well-known "Panpan" trademarks or their main elements. Therefore, the infringing gains of Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang were huge, and the damage suffered by Mou Anju Company was even greater.

In summary, based on Mou Anju Company's request and taking into account the facts of infringement in this case, punitive damages were applied according to law to determine the amount of compensation against Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, Zhou, and others. Regarding the calculation base for punitive damages, Mou Anju Company argued that based on evidence such as the external promotional materials and distribution contracts of Zhou and Xinmou Company, the sales revenue for 2017 was determined to be 200 million yuan, which served as the base amount. Then, using the annual distributor target of at least 50% growth as the standard, the sales revenues for 2017-2019 were determined. Multiplying by the average profit margin of 7.5% for large and medium-sized industrial enterprises in the national furniture manufacturing industry in 2017, and then multiplying by the confusion rate of 48.1% from the public perception market survey report, the calculated base for punitive damages was 34,271,200 yuan, i.e., (200 million + 200 million x 1.5 + 200 million x 1.5 x 1.5) yuan x 7.5% x 48.1% = 34,271,200 yuan. The court of first instance, in the preceding sections, had already analyzed and determined in detail the clear intent to infringe and the serious circumstances of infringement by Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory. After comprehensively considering all evidence in the case, the court of first instance held that the publicity content of Zhou and Xinmou Company regarding an annual output value of 200 million yuan had certain reference value in calculating and determining the amount of compensation. The court of first instance also considered that, while attaching themselves to the commercial reputation of Mou Anju Company's highly well-known trade name and well-known trademarks and causing market confusion, Zhou and Xinmou Company clearly positioned Xinmou Company and its distributors' anti-theft doors and other products at high prices, intentionally raising product prices. Their operating profit would naturally be higher than the average profit margin of large and medium-sized industrial enterprises nationwide. Moreover, the profit margin of 7.5% is the net profit margin after deducting various expenses and costs. For the serious situation where they made infringement their business, if the compensation amount were calculated based on sales profit, the profit margin would be much higher than 7.5%. The 50% growth target for distributors' goods withdrawal was also a conservative indicator. Therefore, this calculation method had a certain theoretical and factual basis, complied with legal provisions, and was relatively scientific and reasonable, and thus was adopted. Accordingly, the base amount for the application of punitive damages against Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory was determined to be 34,271,200 yuan.

Regarding the punitive multiplier. The court of first instance held that the intent to infringe by Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou was very clear, and the circumstances of infringement were quite serious. At the same time, Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou made infringement their business and actually obtained huge profits through the acts of attaching themselves and creating confusion. Therefore, the court of first instance determined that a punitive multiplier of 4 times should be applied. Accordingly, the final amount of compensation should be calculated as 5 times the base amount, i.e., Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou shall compensate Mou Anju Company for the infringement of its exclusive right to use a registered trademark in the amount of 34,271,200 x 5 = 171,356,000 yuan. In fact, for the situation where Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou intentionally infringed, with quite serious circumstances, and made infringement their business, the amount of compensation determined based on their sales profit would be even higher than this amount. Mou Anju Company claimed that Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory should compensate it for losses caused by the infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark in the amount of RMB 95 million, and the court of first instance granted this claim.

(2) Determination of the Amount of Damages for the Unfair Competition Acts

Mou Anju Company claimed that Xinmou Company and others should compensate it for losses caused by the unfair competition acts in the amount of RMB 5 million. The court of first instance held that although the false advertising and commercial defamation unfair competition acts carried out by Xinmou Company, Zhou, and Gumou Door Factory had relative independence, the purpose of carrying out the false advertising and commercial defamation was also to attach themselves to and use Mou Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name and the series of trademarks involved in the case. In actual business operations, the use of the "Xin Panpan" trade name, enterprise name and its abbreviation by Zhou, Xinmou Company, and Gumou Door Factory overlapped with the use of the commercial marks related to "Xin Panpan." The panda mascot image they used corresponded to the panda image in Mou Anju Company's well-known trademark. The revenue obtained and the consequences caused by their use of the Chinese characters, pinyin and their abbreviations, and related marks from the series of trademarks involved in the case to engage in trademark infringement, and their use of enterprise names and abbreviations, trade names, and panda images to engage in unfair competition acts, were identical and mixed, and objectively could not be distinguished or separated. Therefore, considering the subjective degree of intent of Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou and the severity of the infringement circumstances, the claim of Mou Anju Company that Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou should compensate it for losses caused by the unfair competition acts in the amount of RMB 5 million was supported.

(3) Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou Shall Bear Joint and Several Liability for Compensation

Xinmou Company, Gumou Door Factory, and Zhou jointly committed the acts of trademark infringement and unfair competition in this case, and shall jointly and severally compensate Mou Anju Company for losses in the amount of RMB 100 million. Mou Anju Company has already waived its claim for compensation against Zhumou Commercial Firm during the litigation, and the court of first instance granted this waiver.

(4) Determination of the Amount of Reasonable Expenses

Mou Anju Company claimed that XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, Zhou, and ZhuMou Firm should also bear the reasonable expenses it incurred to stop the infringement, including attorney fees, investigation fees, printing fees, notarization fees, travel expenses, etc., totaling RMB 898,212.52. Upon review, the expense receipts submitted by Mou Anju Company had the following issues: (1) Mou Anju Company had explicitly agreed to deduct the notarization fee of RMB 1,190 for the use labeled "clothing and accessories," round-trip airfare of RMB 2,429 from Beijing to Seoul, and high-speed rail ticket of RMB 835 from Hankou to Beijing West Station. The meal expense of RMB 1,491 issued by the Second Branch of Beijing ChaoMou Catering Co., Ltd. on February 19, 2019, the printing fee of RMB 3,242.7 invoiced on May 6, 2019, and the notarization fee of RMB 7,000 invoiced on March 7, 2019 were claimed repeatedly by Mou Anju Company. (2) A considerable portion of the investigation fees and notarization fees involved relatively large individual amounts. Mou Anju Company only provided invoices, from which the actual expenditure details and purposes could not be discerned. Based solely on the amounts shown on the invoices, the notarization fees were clearly excessive. (3) Some notarization acts in places such as Yancheng and Changsha were not carried out by local notarial offices but by notarial offices in Beijing. The notarization fees claimed by Mou Anju Company included travel and other expenses of the notaries. If the notarization had been carried out by local notarial offices, these expenses could have been significantly reduced. Therefore, while legally recognizing and adopting the relevant notarized evidence, requiring XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang to bear these expenses would unnecessarily increase their burden. Accordingly, the reasonable expenses that would have been incurred if the notarization had been carried out by a local notarial office should serve as the standard for determining the notarization fees. (4) The necessity and reasonableness of the printing fee of RMB 27,723, the meal expense of RMB 1,830.91 issued by Beijing MouMou Jiahua Hotel Management Co., Ltd., Galaxy Jiahua Hotel on August 15, 2018, the meal expense of RMB 1,491 issued by the Second Branch of Beijing ChaoMou Catering Co., Ltd. on February 19, 2019, and the taxi fares of RMB 1,241.79 and RMB 564.02 incurred on March 7, 2019 and April 22, 2019, respectively, were not explained by Mou Anju Company.

While noting the above circumstances, the court of first instance also considered that: (1) The reasonable expenses necessarily incurred by Mou Anju Company to stop the infringement and for litigation, such as notarization fees, investigation fees, travel expenses, and printing fees, as well as expenses for purchasing infringing goods such as security doors included in some notarization fees, should be supported. (2) This case involved motions challenging jurisdiction, property preservation, party burden of proof and cross-examination, and trial hearings. Mou Anju Company's litigation representatives invested significant effort in the case, conducted considerable investigation and evidence collection, provided evidence materials totaling over 8,000 pages in 11 volumes, most of which were notarized evidence, and wrote over 80 pages of legal submissions, contributing substantial intellectual labor and providing beneficial intellectual support for the trial. The People's Courts encourage and affirm the positive and beneficial role of lawyers in the trial of intellectual property cases, and this factor will be fully considered when determining attorney fees. The attorney fee of RMB 300,000 claimed by Mou Anju Company was supported by corresponding receipts. The amount of the fee was commensurate with the complexity of the case, the professional competence of the lawyers, and the labor expended. The amount of the agency fee was not improper and should be fully supported. Taking into account the above circumstances and factors, the court of first instance supported RMB 650,000 of the reasonable expenses claimed by Mou Anju Company, and based on the infringing circumstances of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, Zhou, and ZhuMou Firm and their roles in the infringement, determined that XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou shall bear joint and several liability to compensate Mou Anju Company for the reasonable expenses of RMB 650,000 incurred to stop the infringement, and that Fang, the owner of ZhuMou Firm, shall bear joint and several liability with XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou for the aforementioned reasonable expenses within the limit of RMB 50,000.

In summary, the alleged infringing acts and unfair competition acts of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, Zhou, and ZhuMou Firm were established, and they shall bear corresponding legal liability. Pursuant to Articles 13, 14, 48, Items (2), (3), and (7) of Article 57, Article 58, and Paragraph 1 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law, Items (2) and (4) of Article 6, Paragraph 1 of Article 8, Article 11, and Article 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, Article 8 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 64, 119, and 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks, and Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Punitive Damages in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Intellectual Property Rights, the judgment is as follows: 1. As of the effective date of this judgment, XinMou Company and GuMou Door Factory shall immediately cease using the words "Pan Pan", the Pinyin and abbreviations thereof, the panda graphic, and the panda mascot image, and other identifiers associated with Mou Anju Company's "Pan Pan" series trademarks and enterprise name, on the goods they produce or sell and their packaging, in-store decorations, domain names, and in all other business operations and promotions. Fang shall immediately cease selling the infringing products bearing the above words and identifiers, and cease using the above words and identifiers in the decoration of its storefront. 2. XinMou Company shall immediately deregister the website domain name within fifteen days from the effective date of this judgment. 3. XinMou Company shall immediately change its enterprise name within fifteen days from the effective date of this judgment, and the changed enterprise name shall not contain the words "Pan Pan". 4. XinMou Company and Zhou shall immediately cease the acts of false publicity and commercial defamation against Mou Anju Company as of the effective date of this judgment. 5. XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou shall, within fifteen days from the effective date of this judgment, publish an announcement in the *China Market Regulation News* to eliminate the adverse effects (the content shall be reviewed by the court of first instance; if they fail to perform within the time limit, the court of first instance will publish the main contents of this judgment, and the expenses incurred shall be borne by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou). 6. XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou shall, within fifteen days from the effective date of this judgment, jointly and severally compensate Mou Anju Company for losses of RMB 100 million and reasonable expenses of RMB 650,000. Fang shall bear joint and several liability for the aforementioned reasonable expenses within the limit of RMB 50,000. 7. The other claims of Mou Anju Company are rejected. If the obligation to pay a sum of money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 546,291.06 and the preservation fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 551,291.06, shall be borne by XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou in the amount of RMB 501,291.06, and by Fang in the amount of RMB 50,000.

5.
