This Court finds that the issues in dispute between the parties during the second instance are: whether the alleged acts of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou constitute infringement of Mou Anju Company's exclusive right to use the involved series trademarks and unfair competition; and if so, whether the amount of compensation determined by the court of first instance is appropriate.

I. Regarding whether the alleged acts of XinMou Company, GuMou Door Factory, and Zhou constitute infringement of Mou Anju Company's exclusive right to use the involved series trademarks.

Paragraph 2 of Article 57 of the Trademark Law provides: "Without the consent of the trademark registrant, using a trademark that is similar to the registered trademark on the same goods, or using a trademark that is identical or similar to the registered trademark on similar goods, which is likely to cause confusion; selling goods that infringe the exclusive right to use a registered trademark; ... causing other damage to another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark ... shall constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark." Paragraph 1 of Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademark Cases provides: "Using characters identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as the name of an enterprise prominently on identical or similar goods, which is likely to cause misidentification among the relevant public, constitutes an act of causing other damage to another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark as provided in paragraph 7 of Article 57 of the Trademark Law." The legislative purpose of the Trademark Law of China is to strengthen trademark management, protect the exclusive right to use trademarks, encourage producers and operators to ensure the quality of goods and services, maintain trademark reputation, protect the interests of consumers and producers/operators, and promote the development of the socialist market economy. The application for registration and use of trademarks shall follow the principle of good faith. Producers and operators should create and strengthen their own brands through honest business operations, establish visibility commensurate with their own business reputation, continuously enhance the brand value of trademarks and corporate competitiveness, and promote the long-term development of the enterprise.

First, with respect to the degree of recognition of the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company. Mou Anju Company enjoys the exclusive right to use the trademark No. 64** "", No. 130 "", No. 140 "", and No. 1079 "" on goods such as security doors or metal doors. According to the facts found by the trial court, the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company have been registered and used in China for more than 20 years, with a huge scale of operations, products covering the whole country, and the sales volume and market share of security door products ranking first in the industry for more than 20 consecutive years, having obtained at least 157 awards and honors. Although two of the trademark designs are panda patterns from nature, and the panda "Panpan" was the mascot of the 1990 Asian Games, through continuous promotion and use by Mou Anju Company, the involved series of trademarks have a high degree of popularity, reputation, and influence on goods such as "security doors, metal doors, metal windows," have acquired distinctiveness as trademarks, and have a strong trademark identification function. The above four series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company are currently in valid and effective legal status, among which Trademark No. 64, No. 130, and No. 1079** have been repeatedly recognized as well-known trademarks by the China National Intellectual Property Administration and the Beijing Intellectual Property Court. Therefore, the trial court's determination that the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company have reached the level of well-known trademarks and should be protected as well-known trademarks under the Trademark Law of China is not improper.

Second, with respect to the determination of similarity between the accused infringing mark and the involved series of trademarks. The involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company contain elements such as the Chinese character "Panpan," the pinyin "PANPAN," and the panda pattern, and are pronounced as "Panpan." Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Fang, in the production and sale of goods and their packaging, storefront signs or interior decoration, domain names, promotional materials, exhibitions, outdoor advertisements, or other fields, prominently and extensively used the accused infringing mark, producing, selling, and promoting "Xin Panpan" security doors, metal doors and windows, and other goods for business operations. The accused infringing mark is pronounced as "Xin Panpan," which completely includes the pronunciation "Panpan" of the involved series of trademarks, so the pronunciation of the accused infringing mark is similar to that of the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company. The accused infringing mark itself or its main prominent part is the Chinese characters "Xin Panpan," which are similar to the main prominent part "Panpan" of the involved series of trademarks. Some accused infringing marks also use a combination of "Xin Panpan" and a panda pattern; in addition to the similarity between its Chinese characters "Xin Panpan" and the main identification part "Panpan" of the involved series of trademarks, the panda pattern is also similar to the panda pattern in the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company. At the same time, Xin Mou Company also included the Chinese character "Panpan," which is the main identification part of the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company, as the main component of its trade name, and prominently used the abbreviation or trade name of the enterprise, constituting trademark use. Therefore, the trial court's determination that the accused infringing mark used by Xin Mou Company constitutes a similar mark to the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company is also not improper.

Third, with respect to the determination of similarity between the goods for which the involved series of trademarks are approved for use and the goods on which the accused infringing mark is used. The involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company are mainly approved for use on goods in Class 6, such as security doors and metal doors. Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang used the accused infringing mark on goods such as security doors, metal doors and windows, aluminum alloy doors and windows, and smart locks, and the goods on which the two are used constitute identical or similar goods. In addition, Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang also used the accused infringing mark on goods or services such as smart homes and sunrooms, which belong to the same building decoration industry as the goods for which the involved series of trademarks are approved for use, and have strong correlations in terms of production departments, sales channels, sales venues, consumer targets, functions, and uses. Even if the two do not constitute similar goods or services, when the involved series of trademarks have reached the level of well-known trademarks, cross-class protection may be achieved.

Finally, the use of the accused infringing mark causes confusion or misidentification among the relevant public. As mentioned above, the involved series of trademarks have a high degree of awareness and influence. Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang used the accused infringing mark on identical, similar, or highly related goods, which may cause the relevant public to be confused as to the source of the goods or services, or mistakenly believe that there is a specific connection between Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang and Mou Anju Company. With reference to the market survey report provided by Mou Anju Company, 48.1% of the relevant public believed that there is an association between the accused infringing product and the security doors produced and sold by Mou Anju Company, and actual confusion or misidentification has occurred among the relevant public. Therefore, the trial court's determination that Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang's use of the accused infringing mark on identical, similar, or highly related goods or services may cause confusion or misidentification among the relevant public is not improper.

In addition, Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou argued that they acquired the "Xin Panpan" trademark in July 2016, and before the trademark was declared invalid by an effective judgment on January 15, 2019, they lawfully enjoyed the registered trademark right of "Xin Panpan," so their use did not constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company. In this regard, this Court holds that, from the specific manner in which Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang used the accused infringing mark, they did not use the "Xin Panpan" mark in a standardized manner. In Xin Mou Company's JD distribution store and the offline product distribution store in Weng'an County, Guizhou Province, the character "Xin" in "Xin Panpan" was omitted, directly using "Panpan security door," or the character "Xin" was used in a very small deformed form in the upper left corner of "Panpan security door," prominently using "Panpan"; Xin Mou Company, in some franchise agreements, directly referred to the series name of the security doors it sold as "Panpan security door"; Xin Mou Company also used "Panpan Phase III (Xin Panpan Chengdu Base)" as its commercial identifier. In this identifier, "Xin Panpan Chengdu Base" is in parentheses, "Phase III" lacks distinctiveness, and "Panpan" should be the distinctive part of the identifier; where Xin Mou Company does not enjoy the panda pattern trademark, it used the panda pattern in combination with "Xin Panpan." In summary, Xin Mou Company's use of the accused infringing mark had obvious malice in riding on the recognition of the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company, so its appeal argument that using its registered trademark does not infringe Mou Anju Company's trademark rights lacks factual basis, and this Court does not support it. The trial court's determination that Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang's use of the accused infringing mark on identical, similar, or highly related goods or services constitutes infringement of the exclusive right to use the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company is not improper.

II. Whether the accused acts of Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou constitute unfair competition

Paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 6 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provide that operators shall not engage in confusing acts such as unauthorized use of another person's enterprise name that has a certain influence (including abbreviations, trade names, etc.), social organization names (including abbreviations, etc.), names (including pen names, stage names, translated names, etc.); and shall not engage in other confusing acts sufficient to cause others to mistakenly believe that the goods are those of another person or that there is a specific connection with another person. Paragraph 1 of Article 8 provides: "Operators shall not make false or misleading commercial publicity regarding the performance, function, quality, sales status, user evaluations, honors received, etc. of their goods, deceiving or misleading consumers." Article 11 provides: "Operators shall not fabricate or disseminate false or misleading information to damage the business reputation or commodity reputation of a competitor." Article 58 of the Trademark Law provides: "Using another person's registered trademark or unregistered well-known trademark as the trade name in an enterprise name, thereby misleading the public and constituting an act of unfair competition, shall be dealt with in accordance with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China."

First, with respect to the use of the trade name "Panpan." As mentioned above, the involved series of trademarks of Mou Anju Company enjoy a high degree of prominence on security doors and metal doors. As early as 2007, Zhou had business dealings with Mou Anju Company. Knowing the prominence and influence of Mou Anju Company's trade name "Panpan" and the involved series of trademarks, Zhou acquired another person's "Xin Panpan" trademark in July 2016, registered and established Xin Mou Company in September 2016, authorized Xin Mou Company to use the "Xin Panpan" trademark on the same day, and Xin Mou Company immediately entrusted Gu Mou Door Factory to produce security doors and other metal door and window series products. As competitors in the same industry as Mou Anju Company, Xin Mou Company and Gu Mou Door Factory, in their business activities, used the enterprise name "Xin Panpan" and its abbreviation and trade name, engaging in the same business as Mou Anju Company, which clearly had malice in riding on the recognition and influence of Mou Anju Company, constituting a free-riding act, objectively causing confusion and misidentification among the relevant public, and constituting unfair competition.

Second, with respect to the use of the panda mascot image. Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou, knowing the prominence and influence of Mou Anju Company's panda mascot image on security doors, still used a similar panda mascot image in promotional activities to promote and advertise security doors, metal doors and windows, and other identical products as those of Mou Anju Company, which is sufficient to cause consumer confusion or misidentification or to mistakenly believe that there is a specific connection with Mou Anju Company, clearly having malice in riding on the recognition and influence of Mou Anju Company, constituting other confusing acts sufficient to cause others to mistakenly believe that the goods are those of another person or that there is a specific connection with another person as provided in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and constituting unfair competition.

Third, with respect to false publicity. Xin Mou Company was established on September 13, 2016, and began using the "Xin Panpan" trademark to produce and sell security doors and related products in 2017. However, on its official website and WeChat public account, it prominently used "SINCE1998," deceiving and misleading consumers into believing that the "Xin Panpan" brand had been used on security doors and metal doors since 1998. Xin Mou Company also, in the process of business promotion, publicized that Zhou used to do business with the boss of Mou Anju Company and later separated, with one part sold abroad to become Assa Abloy Panpan, and the other part remaining in China to become Xin Panpan, and that Zhou and the boss of Mou Anju Company split the money. It also claimed that Xin Mou Company was the high-end product, upgraded product of the Panpan brand, etc., making false or misleading commercial publicity regarding the relationship between Mou Anju Company and Xin Mou Company, and the operation and brand history of Xin Mou Company. After the registration of the "Xin Panpan" trademark on metal doors and windows and other goods was declared invalid, Xin Mou Company still marked "Xin Panpan" as a registered trademark on security doors, metal doors and windows, and other unregistered goods, clearly having malice to deceive or mislead consumers, with the purpose of intentionally causing confusion to enhance its competitive advantage, constituting unfair competition of false publicity.

Finally, with respect to commercial defamation. On its official website and WeChat public account, Xin Mou Company stated that "there are currently incidents in the market imitating our Xin Panpan Chinese national brand, a well-known brand in the door industry, misleading Chinese consumers, openly publicizing the 'Panpan' registered trademark, maliciously altering it to Panpan security door, Panpan security door, which, according to the principle of standardized use of registered trademarks under the Trademark Law, is a serious violation," and listed the trademarks of Mou Anju Company as trademarks that infringe, imitate, are similar to, or illegal with respect to the "Xin Panpan" trademark. Zhou, in the WeChat group "Sichuan Door Industry Association Boss Club" or his WeChat Moments, sent information about the invalidation procedure he initiated against Mou Anju Company's trademark, and commented, "Imperialism will always only fail, always just a paper tiger," "Warm congratulations on the comprehensive victory of the Xin Panpan trademark in Beijing, everyone must share and publicize, everyone should hold their heads high and sell Xin Panpan security doors honorably, high-end series first-line brand of Chinese national brands, warm congratulations on the comprehensive victory of Xin Panpan in the trademark office's cancellation case... the Chinese national brand Xin Panpan will surely win, win, win," etc. The above acts of Xin Mou Company constitute disseminating false or misleading information, damaging the business reputation and commodity reputation of competitor Mou Anju Company, and constitute unfair competition of commercial defamation.

III. Whether the amount of damages determined by the trial court is appropriate

(1) Whether the trial court's determination of damages for trademark infringement is appropriate

Paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law provide: "The amount of damages for infringement of the exclusive right to use a trademark shall be determined based on the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement; if the actual losses are difficult to determine, it may be determined based on the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement; if the losses of the right holder or the profits gained by the infringer are difficult to determine, it shall be reasonably determined by reference to a multiple of the trademark licensing fee. For malicious infringement of the exclusive right to use a trademark, if the circumstances are serious, the amount of damages may be determined at one to five times the amount determined by the above methods. The amount of damages shall include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder to stop the infringement. In determining the amount of damages, if the right holder has made every effort to provide evidence, and the books and materials related to the infringement are mainly in the possession of the infringer, the people's court may order the infringer to provide the books and materials related to the infringement; if the infringer fails to provide or provides false books and materials, the people's court may determine the amount of damages by reference to the right holder's claims and the evidence provided." Paragraph 1 of Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Punitive Damages in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Intellectual Property Rights provides: "If the plaintiff requests punitive damages, it shall specify the amount of damages, the calculation method, and the facts and reasons on which it is based at the time of filing the lawsuit." Paragraph 1 of Article 5 provides: "When determining the amount of punitive damages, the people's court shall, in accordance with the relevant laws, take the plaintiff's actual losses, the defendant's illegal gains, or the profits gained from the infringement as the calculation base. This base does not include the reasonable expenses paid by the plaintiff to stop the infringement; if the law provides otherwise, follow that provision." Paragraph 3 provides: "If the people's court orders the defendant to provide the books and materials related to the infringement in its possession, and the defendant refuses to provide them without justifiable reasons or provides false books and materials, the people's court may determine the calculation base for punitive damages by reference to the plaintiff's claims and evidence. If the circumstances constitute the situation provided in Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law, legal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law." In this case, Mou Anju Company requested at first instance that the amount of damages be determined based on the infringement profits of Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou, explicitly proposed the application of punitive damages, and specified the calculation method and the facts and reasons on which it was based.

1. Determination of the calculation base in the amount of damages for trademark infringement

First, to determine the amount of damages in this case, Mou Anju Company has made every effort to provide evidence, while the books and materials related to the accused infringement are mainly in the possession of Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou. In the court hearing at first instance, Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou explicitly stated that their financial management was very chaotic, there were no standardized financial annual reports, and they could not accurately provide them, so they should bear the legal consequences of failure to provide evidence. During the appeal, although Mou Door Company submitted bank statements of Xin Mou Company for 2017-2019, bank account of Gu Mou Door Factory, bank statements of Gu Mou Door Factory (bank accounts of Zhang Yi and Tan), and statements of Xin Mou Company for March and September 2017, the above evidence, in which the bank statements submitted as those of Gu Mou Door Factory were only the personal bank accounts of Zhang Yi and Tan, is still insufficient to prove the total quantity and sales amount of the accused infringing products produced and sold by Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou. Under such circumstances, the calculation base for the amount of damages may be determined by reference to Mou Anju Company's claimed infringement profits and the evidence provided.

Second, based on the evidence submitted by Mou Anju Company at first instance, the trial court determined the calculation base for the amount of damages by reference to the following three factors: first, Zhou's external publicity at the "Xin Panpan Group 2018 New Product Annual Meeting and New Retail Summit Forum" in April 2018 that Xin Mou Company planned to achieve output value of one billion yuan in the first five-year plan and five billion yuan in the second five-year plan; second, the statement of Jing, Administrative Director of Xin Mou Company's "Shared Cloud Decoration Group," at the 2018 Beijing International Building Materials Exhibition that the national annual sales of "Xin Panpan doors" reached RMB 200 million; third, the agency contracts provided by Xin Mou Company with its distributors, most of which stipulated that the annual target for picking up goods would increase by at least 50%. Combining the above three factors, the trial court determined the output value for the first year as RMB 200 million, and calculated the output value for the first three years (2017-2019) of Xin Mou Company, Gu Mou Door Factory, and Zhou as 2 + 2×1.5 + 2×1.5×1.5 = RMB 950 million. If calculated according to the above method, the output value for the fourth year would be 2×1.5×1.5×1.5 = RMB 675 million, and for the fifth year would be 2×1.5×1.5×1.5×1.5 = RMB 1.0125 billion, so the total output value for the first five years would be RMB 2.6375 billion. There is a significant gap between the result calculated by the above method and Zhou's external publicity of RMB 1 billion for the first five years. On one hand, the trial court referred to Zhou's claimed RMB 1 billion for the first five years when determining the calculation base for the amount of damages; on the other hand, the trial court calculated the output value for the first five years according to its own calculation method as RMB 2.6375 billion, so the above calculation method of the trial court contains a logical error. In addition, when determining the calculation base for the amount of damages, the trial court determined the degree of public confusion based on the 48.1% of respondents who believed that there was a correlation between the security doors of Xin Mou Company and Mou Anju Company as derived from the survey report commissioned by Mou Anju Company from Beijing XX Market Research Co., Ltd., which lacks legal basis. In summary, this Court corrects the calculation method used by the trial court to determine the calculation base for the amount of damages.

Third, with reference to Zhou's statement at the summit forum that Xin Company planned to achieve a first five-year output value of one billion yuan and the factor that the dealer agency contract stipulated an annual growth rate of 50%, this Court calculated that Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou had an output value of RMB 76 million in 2017, RMB 114 million in 2018 (76 million × 1.5 = 114 million), and RMB 171 million in 2019 (76 million × 1.5 × 1.5 = 171 million), totaling RMB 361 million for the three years. According to the above calculation method, the output value in the fourth year would be RMB 256.5 million (76 million × 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.5 = 256.5 million), and the output value in the fifth year would be RMB 384.75 million (76 million × 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.5 = 384.75 million), so the total output value for the first five years would be RMB 1,002.25 million. The conclusion reached by the above calculation method is basically consistent with Zhou's external publicity of a first five-year output value of one billion yuan. Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou argued that the first five-year output value of one billion yuan and the annual growth rate of 50% stipulated in the dealer agency contract were both planned targets to be achieved and could not be used as the basis for determining their output value from 2017 to 2019. In this regard, this Court is of the opinion that Jing, the Administrative Director of Xin Company's "Shared Cloud Decoration Group," stated at the 2018 Beijing International Building Materials Exhibition that the national annual sales performance of "Xin Panpan Doors" was two hundred million yuan. This was not a planned target but an already achieved operating performance, and it specifically referred to the actual completed annual sales performance of the Xin Panpan brand doors. It did not include the sales performance of other products under the Xin Panpan brand, such as sunrooms and smart homes, nor did it include the sales performance of other brand doors produced by Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou. If calculated based on the actual annual performance of two hundred million yuan that Jing publicly claimed to have achieved, even without considering the annual growth rate, the sum of the output value of Xin Panpan doors from 2017 to 2019 would reach RMB 600 million. However, the output values for the three years 2017-2019 calculated by setting the first year's output value at RMB 76 million were RMB 76 million, RMB 114 million, and RMB 171 million respectively. None of these individual years reached the RMB 200 million actual annual output value that Jing claimed to have completed, and the three-year total was only RMB 361 million. This calculation method is more consistent with Zhou's external publicity of a first five-year output value of one billion yuan and does not exceed the level of Xin Panpan door output value that Jing of Xin Company publicly claimed to have completed in one year, making it relatively more reasonable. The explanation submitted by Menye Company during the second instance, in which Jing stated that he had misunderstood the sales volume and production volume of "Xin Panpan" doors, is insufficient to overturn the performance statement he publicly released at the Beijing International Building Materials Exhibition. This Court does not accept this evidence.

Finally, from the information released by Zhou in the "Sichuan Door and Window Association Boss Club" WeChat group and his WeChat Moments, the Xin Panpan security door is positioned as a high-end series, a first-line brand. Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou clearly positioned their security doors, metal doors, and other products at high prices to increase their product prices. At the 2018 Beijing International Building Materials Exhibition, Jing, the Administrative Director of Xin Company's "Shared Cloud Decoration Group," stated that Xin Company was the high-end product of Panpan. Furthermore, the allegedly infringing marks used by Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou included "Xin Panpan High-End Door" and "Xin Panpan High-End Security Door." It can be seen from this that the operating profit of the Xin Panpan brand would not be lower than the average profit rate of large and medium-sized industrial enterprises nationwide. The original trial court calculated the profit of Xin Panpan brand products using the 2017 average profit rate of large and medium-sized furniture manufacturing enterprises nationwide, which was 7.5%, and this would not exceed their actual profit. Therefore, this Court determines that the calculation base for the amount of compensation for trademark infringement in this case is (76 million + 76 million × 1.5 + 76 million × 1.5 × 1.5) yuan × 7.5% = RMB 27,075,000.

2. Determination of the multiplier for punitive damages for trademark infringement

Article 9 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in Cases of Jurisdiction over Trademark Cases and the Application of Law after the Implementation of the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law provides: "Unless otherwise provided in this Interpretation, for trademark civil cases accepted by a people's court after the implementation of the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law, if the case involves conduct that occurred before the implementation of the Decision, the provisions of the Trademark Law before the amendment shall apply; if it involves conduct that occurred before the implementation of the Decision and continued after the implementation of the Decision, the provisions of the Trademark Law after the amendment shall apply." Article 6, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Punitive Damages in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Intellectual Property provides: "When a people's court determines the multiplier for punitive damages in accordance with the law, it shall comprehensively consider factors such as the degree of subjective fault of the defendant and the seriousness of the circumstances of the infringement." Subparagraphs (1) and (4) of Article 3, paragraph 2 provide: "If the defendant continues to commit the infringing act after being notified or warned by the plaintiff or an interested party; or if the defendant had business dealings with the plaintiff or an interested party or had engaged in consultations to reach a contract, etc., and had been exposed to the infringed intellectual property right, the people's court may preliminarily determine that the defendant had the intention to infringe the intellectual property right." Article 4, paragraph 1 provides: "For the determination of the seriousness of circumstances of an intellectual property infringement, the people's court shall comprehensively consider factors such as the means and frequency of infringement, the duration, geographical scope, scale, and consequences of the infringement, and the conduct of the infringer in the litigation." Subparagraph (5) of paragraph 2 provides: "If the infringer's profit or the right holder's loss is huge, the people's court may determine that the circumstances are serious." In this case, based on Anju Company's request at first instance and the facts of the infringement in this case, punitive damages should be applied to Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou to determine the amount of compensation for trademark infringement. Given that the alleged infringing acts in this case continued until 2019, the original trial court properly applied the amended Article 63, paragraph 1 of the Trademark Law of 2019 and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Punitive Damages in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Intellectual Property as the basis for determining the multiplier of punitive damages in this case.

Regarding the determination of infringement intent. First, Chengdu Wanxiang Gu Technology Co., Ltd., where Zhou served as the legal representative, had business dealings with Anju Company as early as 2007. It can be determined that Zhou was fully aware of the fame and influence of Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name and the series of trademarks involved. Nevertheless, Zhou established Xin Company in September 2016, actively sought to acquire the "Xin Panpan" trademark, authorized Xin Company to use the acquired "Xin Panpan" trademark, and then had Xin Company entrust Gu Door Factory to produce security doors and other metal door and window series products, engaging in the same business as Anju Company. Second, "Xin Panpan" is a homophone for "New Panpan." Xin Company registered the "Xin Panpan" trade name, used the characters "Xin Panpan," its pinyin, or its abbreviation, together with related panda patterns, and claimed that Xin Company and Anju Company had a relationship of "New Panpan" and "Old Panpan," and that "Xin Panpan" security door products were high-end products or upgraded products of the "Panpan" brand. In some franchise agreements, Xin Company directly referred to the security door series it sold as "Panpan security doors." The consignment note for sending security doors and accessories by Xin Company to the owner Fang of Zhu Company Store showed the consignor as "New Panpan." The above conduct of Xin Company clearly had the intention to free-ride on the fame of Anju Company and its series of trademarks involved. Third, Zhou, knowing full well that Anju Company had filed a request for a declaration of invalidity of the "Xin Panpan" trademark on January 19, 2017, nevertheless instructed Xin Company to continue using the allegedly infringing marks. After the trademark administrative authority issued a ruling on November 17, 2017, declaring the "Xin Panpan" trademark invalid, and after the effective judgment of January 15, 2019, upheld the invalidity ruling, Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou continued to use the allegedly infringing marks. Finally, after the effective judgment determined that the "Xin Panpan" trademark should be invalidated, Xin Company briefly renamed its previously registered WeChat public account "Xin Panpan High-End Security Door" to "Xin Pan Ming Pin Premium Security Door" on May 6, 2019, but after three months, it renamed it again to "Sichuan Xin Company Co., Ltd." Therefore, the third and fifth groups of evidence submitted by Menye Company during the second instance are insufficient to prove that Xin Company had stopped using the trademark after the "Xin Panpan" trademark was invalidated. Moreover, even after Xin Company changed its name to Menye Company, it still referred to itself as "Xin Panpan" in the company introduction. In summary, Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou clearly had the intention to infringe Anju Company's series of trademark rights involved.

Regarding the determination of serious circumstances. At the "Xin Panpan Group 2018 New Product Annual Conference and New Retail Summit Forum" in April 2018, Zhou stated, "We plan to open one thousand corporate pavilions within three years," and "We planned to invite 120 dealers today, but we actually have 180 in attendance, and many more are on the way." From the above content declared by Zhou, not including the dealers on the way, the number of dealers actually present reached 180, including dealers from Sichuan, Chongqing, Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hunan, Yunnan, Gansu, Guizhou, and other places affiliated with Xin Company. Xin Company opened franchise stores and directly-operated stores nationwide, conducting online and offline operations and promotions. Based on the contracts it provided, Xin Company developed franchisees in twelve provinces, cities, and counties nationwide, with a large scale of operation and daily production volume. Xin Company's brochures and official website stated that Xin Panpan Artisan Doors are positioned as Chinese door and window artisans, with a total investment of RMB 2 billion, owning six full-owned, invested, controlled, and shared door companies, twelve wooden door companies..., with a total planned land area of 1,000,000 square meters, currently having 3,000,000 security doors..., 2,000,000 sets of matching wooden doors..., three major bases, etc.; it claimed to have jointly developed a fully automatic full-groove Marshal frame production line with the large Chinese door equipment company New Century, with a daily production capacity of 10,000 premium series units per day, ranking first in China; the wooden door company jointly introduced a fully automated production line, with a daily production capacity of 4,000 solid wood doors per day, the highest single-factory production capacity for solid wood doors in China. The doors and windows introduced a fully automatic production line and assembly line from the German company Weger, with automated management series for the door and window industry, making it a model door and window enterprise for China's Industry 4.0, with nearly one hundred physical stores nationwide. From the above facts, Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou had a large scale of infringement, covering a wide geographical area, and obtained huge profits from the infringement. It should be determined that the circumstances of their infringement are serious.

Therefore, comprehensively considering factors such as the degree of subjective fault of Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou, and the seriousness of the circumstances of the infringement, the original trial court properly determined a punitive damages multiplier of 4 times in accordance with the law. That is, the final amount of compensation for trademark infringement is calculated as 5 times the calculation base of RMB 27,075,000: 27,075,000 × 5 = RMB 135,375,000. In its original claim, Anju Company requested Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou to compensate it for losses caused by the infringement of its exclusive right to use the trademark in the amount of RMB 95,000,000. This amount does not exceed the final compensation amount of RMB 135,375,000 determined by this Court and should be fully supported. Although the original trial court improperly determined the calculation base for punitive damages as RMB 34,271,200, leading to an improper determination that Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou should compensate Anju Company in the amount of RMB 171,356,000, the conclusion of fully supporting Anju Company's original claim for compensation for trademark infringement in the amount of RMB 95,000,000 was not improper, and this Court affirms it.

(II) Whether the original trial court's determination of the amount of compensation for the unfair competition acts in this case was appropriate

Article 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "If an operator violates the provisions of this Law and causes damage to others, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law. An operator whose legitimate rights and interests are damaged by an act of unfair competition may file a lawsuit with a people's court. The amount of compensation for an operator damaged by an act of unfair competition shall be determined according to the actual losses suffered by the operator as a result of the infringement; if the actual losses are difficult to calculate, it shall be determined according to the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement. If an operator maliciously implements an act of infringing trade secrets and the circumstances are serious, the amount of compensation may be determined at between one and five times the amount determined according to the above methods. The amount of compensation shall also include the reasonable expenses paid by the operator to stop the infringing act. If, for acts of an operator violating Articles 6 and 9 of this Law, the actual losses suffered by the right holder as a result of the infringement and the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement are difficult to determine, the people's court may, based on the circumstances of the infringement, award compensation of not more than RMB 5,000,000 to the right holder."

In this case, as mentioned above, Xin Company engaged in unfair competition acts such as using Anju Company's trade name and panda mascot image, as well as making false representations and engaging in business defamation, and it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law. In its actual business operations, Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou jointly used the "Xin Panpan" trade name, enterprise name, and its abbreviations for publicity and promotion, and jointly used a panda mascot image highly similar to the panda pattern in the series of trademarks involved in this case owned by Anju Company. The purpose of engaging in false representations and business defamation was also to free-ride on Anju Company's "Panpan" trade name and the series of trademarks involved, in order to achieve the goals of deceiving or misleading consumers, intentionally creating confusion to enhance their competitive advantage, and harming competitors. Therefore, the original trial court's decision to support Anju Company's request for Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou to jointly compensate it for losses caused by the unfair competition acts in the amount of RMB 5,000,000, based on the degree of subjective intent of Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou and the seriousness of the infringement circumstances, was not improper.

Given that Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou jointly committed trademark infringement and unfair competition acts, the original trial court's judgment ordering them to jointly and severally compensate Anju Company for losses in the amount of RMB 100,000,000 was not improper. Anju Company claimed that Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, Zhou, and Fang should bear the reasonable expenses incurred by it to stop the infringing acts and submitted corresponding evidence. The original trial court's determination that Xin Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou should jointly and severally compensate Anju Company for reasonable expenses in the amount of RMB 650,000, and that Fang should bear compensation liability within the scope of RMB 50,000, was also not improper.

In summary, the grounds of appeal of Menye Company, Gu Door Factory, and Zhou are all untenable, and this Court dismisses them. The original trial judgment was improper in determining the calculation base for punitive damages, but the result of the judgment was not improper, and this Court affirms it. Pursuant to Article 48, Article 57, subparagraphs (2), (3), and (7), Article 58, and Articles 63, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 6, subparagraphs (2) and (4), Article 8, paragraph 1, Article 11, and Article 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 8 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Trademark Civil Disputes; Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Punitive Damages in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Intellectual Property; and Article 177, paragraph 1, subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.
